title: Fixing types
summary: Turn text that looks like numbers and dates into real numbers and dates, without crashing on the junk.

steps.title: Why the type matters
body: One bad cell (`"n/a"`, `"$12"`, `"1,200"`) makes `read_csv` load the whole column as **text**. Everything still *looks* fine when printed, but:
So the first cleaning question for every column is: **what type should this be?** Check `df.dtypes`: a numeric column showing `str` or `object` is a red flag.

steps.explain: As text, `"100"` sorts before `"25"` because `"1" < "2"`. After `astype(int)` the order and the sum are numeric.

steps.title: Converting without crashing
body: `astype(float)` stops at the first value it cannot convert. `pd.to_numeric(..., errors="coerce")` turns those values into `NaN` instead, so you can **see** what you lost:
bad = raw[nums.isna() & raw.notna()]         # the values that failed

Strip known decoration first (`$`, `,`, `%`, spaces) with `.str.replace(r"[$,%]", "", regex=True)`, then coerce whatever is left. Count the new `NaN`s: if half the column failed, your cleaning rule is wrong, not the data.

steps.explain: `astype` is strict. Use `pd.to_numeric(s, errors="coerce")` to get `[3.0, NaN]`.

steps.title: Parse prices
prompt: Write `parse_prices(s)` that takes a Series of price **text** like `"$1,200.50"`, `" 30 "`, `"n/a"` and returns a Series of floats:
- remove `$` and `,` characters and surrounding spaces,
- anything that still is not a number becomes `NaN`.
template: Dojo.check("junk becomes NaN", pd.isna(_out.iloc[2]), "'n/a' should become NaN, not crash")
Dojo.check("empty and missing become NaN", bool(_out2.iloc[2:].isna().all()), "empty text should be NaN")

steps.title: Dates
body: Dates as text cannot be compared, subtracted or grouped by month. `pd.to_datetime` converts them; pass `format=` so pandas never guesses whether `03/04/2024` is 3 April or 4 March:
`errors="coerce"` works as with numbers: impossible dates (`31/02/2024`) become `NaT`.

steps.explain: With `%d/%m/%Y`, `03/04/2024` is 3 April. There is no 31 February, so that one becomes `NaT` (its month shows as `nan`, and the other months become floats because of it). From 15 Dec 2023 to 3 Apr 2024 is 110 days.

steps.prompt: Parse US-style dates (`12/31/2024`) and keep just the year.
What type should each column become?
steps.explain: Zip codes and phone numbers are identifiers, not quantities: as numbers you would lose leading zeros and `+`, and their average means nothing.

steps.title: Fix the types
prompt: Write `fix_types(df)` for a DataFrame whose columns all arrived as text: `order_date` (`dd/mm/yyyy`), `qty` (whole numbers, some junk) and `price` (like `"$1,050.00"`). Return a new DataFrame with:
- `price` as floats (`$` and `,` removed, junk becomes `NaN`),
- a new column `month` holding the month number of `order_date`.
hints: Work on `out = df.copy()` and replace one column at a time.
template: Dojo.check("order_date is a datetime column", pd.api.types.is_datetime64_any_dtype(_out["order_date"]), "use pd.to_datetime")
Dojo.check("impossible date becomes NaT", pd.isna(_out["order_date"].iloc[1]), "30/02 does not exist")
Dojo.check("junk qty becomes NaN", pd.isna(_out["qty"].iloc[1]), "'two' should be NaN")
Dojo.check("junk price becomes NaN", pd.isna(_out["price"].iloc[2]), "'free' should be NaN")
